slides.heading: Why Loops Matter
slides.body: Why Loops Matter is part of Indefinite Iteration. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Why Loops Matter
slides.body: Loops repeat instructions. Indefinite iteration uses a condition to decide when the repetition should stop.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A loop is like washing dishes until the sink is empty. You may not know the exact number at the start, but the condition tells you when to stop.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Every while loop needs a condition that can eventually become False, unless you intentionally stop it with break.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use a while loop to print 1, 2, and 3.
slides.hint: The condition can be count <= 3. Remember to increase count.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Write a while loop that prints 1 to 4.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
